subject: MedGrove DPA: data transfer zoning & subprocessor access scope
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medgrove.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@medgrove.com>, MedGrove Legal <legal@medgrove.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: MedGrove DPA: data transfer zoning & subprocessor access scope

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the call earlier — MedGrove's security team has a few follow-ups as we finalize the DPA negotiation. To keep our legal and engineering reviews aligned, can you confirm the following?

1) Which subprocessors have access to customer PII in the inference path (tokenization/proxy, model serving, telemetry exports)? Please list the operational role and the region where that subprocessor operates.

2) Do you offer per-customer KMS (BYOK) for key custody of PII-at-rest? If not, what controls do you provide around key separation and access audits?

3) We need an updated dataflow diagram that clearly shows where raw PII may transit or get persisted, and how pseudonymization/redaction is applied. Can you attach the most recent diagram and a short legend?

If you could please reply with a short bulleted response and attachments today, our legal team will incorporate into the DPA redlines.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Security & Privacy
MedGrove Health

P.S. Aaron is on the thread to help with any infra-level details.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medgrove.com>
Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@medgrove.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: MedGrove DPA: data transfer zoning & subprocessor access scope

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, attachments below.

1) Subprocessors & operational roles (inference/evidence):
- Model infra: VertexPoolOps LLC (us-west-2) — manages multi-tenant GPU pools in Dedicated mode (only for Hosted customers when not using Private).
- Tokenization/proxy layer: Redwood-side proxy service (managed by Redwood) — located in Redwood US and EU regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1). No external third party has raw access to tokens except VertexPoolOps for runtime compute.
- Telemetry & analytics: LogHarbor Inc. (us-central1) — receives anonymized usage telemetry; PII is redacted before export.

2) KMS / key custody:
- We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated contracts via integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). For standard Hosted customers we use Redwood-managed KMS with strict key separation per-tenant and HSM-backed storage; key access is logged and audited.

3) Dataflow diagram & legend: attached 'dataflow-v2.png' shows request ingress, tokenization proxy, model serving, KV cache, and telemetry export paths. Legend clarifies which components touch raw input, which operate on pseudonymized tokens, and where persisted artifacts exist.

Notes / mitigations:
- Pseudonymization: we apply prefix tokenization + optional redaction at the proxy for fields marked as PII in the incoming schema — configurable per-customer.
- Export controls: telemetry exports are configurable; by default they contain aggregated counters and latency metrics. Any customer-level payloads are blocked unless explicit export is enabled via an admin flag.
- Cross-border: routing policies are region-aware; customer can opt to restrict to a single region in Dedicated/Private. Hosted defaults to closest-region routing with opt-out.

Attachments: medgrove-ssq-answers.pdf (attached), dataflow-v2.png (attached).

Let us know if you want a short video walkthrough; Kimberly and Jonas are looped for any technical follow-ups.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: medgrove-ssq-answers.pdf (PDF, 18 pages)
Attachment: dataflow-v2.png (PNG, diagram)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: MedGrove DPA: data transfer zoning & subprocessor access scope

On 2028-12-02 12:40, Rachel Kim wrote:
> Pseudonymization: we apply prefix tokenization + optional redaction at the proxy for fields marked as PII in the incoming schema — configurable per-customer.

Hi Lena — quick infra points from my side:
- Encryption-at-rest: all persisted artifacts (model caches, logs, stored prompts when customer opts in) are encrypted with KMS-managed keys. For Dedicated customers we can bind to your KMS key ARN; for Hosted customers we offer tenant-scoped keys.
- Key access: only a small ops role (key-ops) has access to KMS management APIs and all calls are logged to audit trails with 90-day retention (longer retention available as an add-on).
- BYOK availability: BYOK for Hosted is not currently available in our standard plan; it's supported for Dedicated and Private. If MedGrove requires Hosted-BYOK we can propose an enterprise addendum as part of the DPA.

I've attached an initial redline placeholder (dpa-redlines.docx) that flags BYOK language and audit-term requests.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dpa-redlines.docx (DOCX, 6 pages)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medgrove.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-12-03T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: MedGrove DPA: data transfer zoning & subprocessor access scope

Lena / team — adding a few operational clarifications to help your infra reviewers:

- Region routing rules: requests are routed by policy (latency-first by default). For MedGrove we can pin inference traffic to us-west-2 only (no cross-border routing) under Dedicated/Private. Hosted will require an explicit region restriction clause.
- KV cache: inferences use a per-request KV cache that may store ephemeral tokens for model context; cached content is TTL-bound (<24h) unless customer opts into longer session retention. Cache persistence locations are shown in dataflow-v2.png.
- Telemetry redaction: telemetry pipeline strips any fields labeled PII at the proxy level. For extra defense-in-depth we offer an optional scrubber stage that hashes certain identifiers before log export.

If helpful, I can export a slightly annotated dataflow that highlights the PII redaction gates — happy to share in a short screen share.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
